narrative: OMX30 opens into a mixed macro backdrop where global equity weakness (-0.346% correlation signal) and elevated US yields (4.837%, +65bps) conflict with Sweden's domestic bull regime (+5.9% vs 200-MA). While long-term positioning remains constructive, today's technicals reveal fragility: ADX weakness (12.0) suppresses confidence, MACD has rolled below signal with negative histogram (-6.291), and price sits in the lower half of Bollinger bands. The IMF tariff headlines and trade tension narrative weigh on sentiment despite commodity strength (Brent +1.13%, gold +0.50%), which should support miners but pressures industrials on input cost fears. Expect choppy, range-bound trade with low conviction.
morningBrief: OMX30 starts Thursday with a cautious tone amid conflicting signals. Global equities down overnight (DAX -0.19%, S&P -0.48%) and VIX creeping higher to 16.49 suggest light risk-off sentiment, even as commodity strength (oil +1.13%, copper +0.29%) would normally support export-heavy index. Key watch: US 10Y yields up 65bps to 4.837% — positive for bank NIM but negative DCF drag on tech/telecom (Ericsson, Hexagon at risk from NASDAQ weakness). ADX at 12.0 (weak) cuts our tactical confidence by 30%; treat any moves as choppy range noise until 3180 resistance (50-MA) is tested. Watch USD/SEK steady at 9.595 (+0.13%) — light tailwind for Volvo/Atlas on export side but offset by oil input costs. Boliden only bright spot (gold+copper upside). Avoid chasing; stay defensive until ADX inflects above 18.
